answers.answer: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest is encrypted using AES-256 or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering. This covers production databases and their read replicas, object storage (Amazon S3) used for customer data, staging, and exports, block storage volumes attached to production compute, backups and snapshots, and log storage. Encryption at rest is applied by default at the storage layer: engineers may not create production storage resources with encryption disabled, and automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources. Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

- Production databases and their read replicas
- Object storage (Amazon S3) used for customer data, staging, and exports
- Block storage volumes attached to production compute
- Backups and snapshots
- Log storage

Encryption at rest is applied by default at the storage layer. Engineers may not create production storage resources with encryption disabled. Automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources.
Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

answers.answer: Yes. Every Tidewell-issued laptop must be enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system and have full-disk encryption enabled, both before it is issued and at all times afterward. Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically. If a laptop is not fixed within 3 days, it loses access to corporate systems until it is compliant again.

Our documents do not say whether the full penetration test report can be shared under NDA. Only the summary letter is listed as available.

answers.reasoning_note: The Trust Center (KB-01) lists only the summary letter, available on request. No source covers sharing the full report under NDA, so a human must confirm. Only the SOC 2 report is listed as available under NDA. KB-32's 2024 answer citing an October 2023 test is outdated.

No passage mentions a 24/7 SOC or round-the-clock staffing. Related: KB-06 v1.4 §7 says automated detection rules send alerts to the Security team's queue; KB-10 v2.0 §6.2 sets triage targets (SEV1 in 30 min). Neither confirms 24/7 coverage.

answers.answer: Our current Information Security Policy (v3.2) does not name a CISO role. The Head of Security "owns the security program day to day" and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly. The Chief Technology Officer is the accountable executive for the information security program. A Security & Compliance team implements and monitors security controls. Our documents give neither the name of the person in the Head of Security role nor the size of the security team.

citations.passage: **Head of Security.** Owns the security program day to day. Maintains this policy and its supporting standards, oversees risk assessments, leads security incident response, and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly.
**Chief Technology Officer (CTO).** Accountable executive for the information security program.
**Security & Compliance team.** Implements and monitors security controls, manages the SOC 2 program, responds to customer security questionnaires, and supports audits.

answers.reasoning_note: Partial answer: KB-02 v3.2 covers security leadership roles but gives no name or team headcount. Superseded KB-03 v2.4 and the 2024 answer library (KB-32) both say the Director of Engineering owns the program; that is outdated and not used.
